errors.text: The hypothesis does not identify the AlCoCrFeNi2.1 as-cast FCC+B2 eutectic alloy or its relevant phase structure.
It replaces the target intermediate-temperature aging response with an unspecified precipitation-strengthening intervention.
The proposed 1000°C exposure misses the approximately 550–750°C transition window and the critical 600°C embrittlement and 750°C recovery conditions.
It predicts simple mitigation rather than the observed non-monotonic ductile–brittle–ductile transition.
It omits the coupled L12 ordering, increased APBE/modulus, restricted cross-slip, planar slip, jagged B2/FCC phase boundaries, and crack initiation mechanism.
The cited evidence supports elevated-temperature strength from precipitation, not preservation of toughness after thermal exposure or retention of the original strength–ductility combination.
